questions.problem:
Given that the differential equation 

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}-4y=5\operatorname{sin}⁡x
$$

has the complementary solution ${y}_{c}(x)=A{e}^{4x}$, find the particular solution ${y}_{p}(x)$ to this equation.

${y}_{p}(x)=$
{{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
To find the general solution of an inhomogeneous first-order linear equation with constant coefficients on the left-hand side, we must find the sum of the complementary and particular solutions.

The right-hand side of the inhomogeneous equation is $5\operatorname{sin}⁡x.$ So, we assume the particular solution to be 

$$
{y}_{p}(x)=\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡x+\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡x.
$$

where $\alpha $ and $\beta $ are constants to be determined. 

Calculating the first derivative of ${y}_{p}$ gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}{y}_{p}}{\text{d}x}=-\alpha \operatorname{sin}⁡x+\beta \operatorname{cos}⁡x.
$$

To find the values of $\alpha $ and $\beta ,$ we substitute ${y}_{p}$ and ${y}_{p}^{′}$ into the differential equation:

$$
(-\alpha \operatorname{sin}⁡x+\beta \operatorname{cos}⁡x)-4(\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡x+\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡x)=5\operatorname{sin}⁡x.
$$

Grouping the terms on the left-hand side gives

$$
(\beta -4\alpha )\operatorname{cos}⁡x+(-\alpha -4\beta )\operatorname{sin}⁡x=5\operatorname{sin}⁡x.
$$

Equating the coefficients, we get the following system of equations:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}\beta -4\alpha =0\, & (\text{equating the coefficients of}\,\operatorname{cos}⁡x) \\ -\alpha -4\beta =5\, & (\text{equating the coefficients of}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡x)\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Solving this system gives $\alpha =-\frac{5}{17},$ $\beta =-\frac{20}{17}.$

Therefore, the particular solution ${y}_{p}(x)$ is

$$
{y}_{p}(x)=-\frac{5}{17}\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)-\frac{20}{17}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x).
$$

$$
3\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}-6y=4\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x).
$$

Find the general solution to this equation given that the complementary solution is ${y}_{c}(x)=A{e}^{2x},$ where $A$ is an arbitrary constant.

$y(x)=A{e}^{2x}\,+\,($
{{field-1}}
$)\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)\,+\,($
{{field-2}}
$)\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)$

To find the general solution of an inhomogeneous first-order linear equation with constant coefficients on the left-hand side, we must find the sum of the complementary and particular solutions.

To find the complementary solution ${y}_{c}$ we solve the corresponding homogeneous equation, given by

$$
3\frac{\text{d}{y}_{c}}{\text{d}x}-6{y}_{c}=0.
$$

Solving this equation, we find that the complementary solution is

$$
{y}_{c}=A{e}^{2x}
$$

where $A$ is an arbitrary constant.

We now need to find the particular solution ${y}_{p}(x).$

The right-hand side of the inhomogeneous equation is $4\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x).$ So, we assume the particular solution to be 

$$
{y}_{p}(x)=\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)+\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡(2x).
$$

where $\alpha $ and $\beta $ are constants that are to be determined. 

Calculating the first derivative of ${y}_{p}$ gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}{y}_{p}}{\text{d}x}=-2\alpha \operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)+2\beta \operatorname{cos}⁡(2x).
$$

To find the values of $\alpha $ and $\beta ,$ we substitute ${y}_{p}$ and ${y}_{p}^{′}$ into the differential equation:

$$
3(-2\alpha \operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)+2\beta \operatorname{cos}⁡(2x))-6(\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)+\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡(2x))=4\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)
$$

Grouping the terms on the left-hand side gives

$$
(-6\alpha +6\beta )\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)+(-6\alpha -6\beta )\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)=4\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x).
$$

Equating the coefficients, we get the following system of equations:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}-6\alpha +6\beta =4\, & (\text{equating the coefficients of}\,\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)) \\ -6\alpha -6\beta =0\, & (\text{equating the coefficients of}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x))\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Solving this system gives $\alpha =-\frac{1}{3},\beta =\frac{1}{3}.$

Therefore, 

$$
{y}_{p}(x)=-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)+\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x).
$$

The general solution is given by

$$
y(x)={y}_{c}(x)+{y}_{p}(x),
$$

and therefore, the general solution in our case is

$$
y=A{e}^{2x}+(-\frac{1}{3})\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)+(\frac{1}{3})\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x).
$$

To find the general solution of an inhomogeneous first-order linear equation with constant coefficients on the left-hand side, we must find the sum of the complementary and particular solutions.

The right-hand side of the inhomogeneous equation is $2\cos{x}.$ So, we assume the particular solution to be 

$$
y_p(x) = \alpha \cos x + \beta  \sin x,
$$

where $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are constants to be determined. 

Calculating the first derivative of $y_p$ gives

$$
\frac{\textrm{d}y_p}{\textrm{d}x} =   - \alpha \sin {x} +  \beta \cos {x}.
$$

To find the values of $\alpha$ and $\beta,$ we substitute $y_p$ and $y_p'$ into the differential equation:

$$
( - \alpha \sin {x} +  \beta \cos {x}) + 3(\alpha \cos x + \beta  \sin x) = 2\cos{x}.
$$

Grouping the terms on the left-hand side gives

$$
(3\alpha+\beta)\cos x + (-\alpha + 3\beta) \sin x = 2\cos{x}.
$$

Equating the coefficients, we get the following system of equations:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}3\alpha +\beta =2\, & (\text{equating the coefficients of}\,\operatorname{cos}⁡x) \\ -\alpha +3\beta =0\, & (\text{equating the coefficients of}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡x)\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Solving this system gives $\alpha = \dfrac 3 5,$ $\beta = \dfrac 1 5.$

Therefore, the particular solution $y_p(x)$ is

$$
y_p(x) = \dfrac{3}{5} \cos(x) + \dfrac{1}{5} \sin(x).

$$
y_p(x) = \alpha \cos(3x) + \beta  \sin(3x),
$$

where $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are constants that are to be determined.
